n: Thomas B. Marsh, a recent convert who had come to Palmyra after hearing of the Book of Mormon, is blessed for his faith. He later became the first President of the Quorum of the Twelve.

f.g: Thomas B. Marsh, baptized September 1830; he left the Church in 1838 and returned in 1857.

n: Thomas has suffered because of family opposition, but the Lord promises his family will come to believe and join him in the Church.
Thomas’s mission begins now; his tongue will be freed to share “glad tidings of great joy” — the angels’ words at Jesus’ birth.
He will preach the revelations given to Joseph, reaping in a field ready for harvest — and ready to be burned if not harvested.

f.g: a variation on the harvest image: the field is ripe and urgent, facing judgment if not gathered.

n: Working with all his soul, Thomas’s sins are forgiven, and he will be loaded with harvested “sheaves” (converts). The laborer deserves his pay, so his family will be provided for.

f.w: laden with sheaves upon your back
the laborer is worthy of his hire

n: He need leave his family only for short periods; the Lord will prepare a place for them.
God will open hearts to receive Thomas and establish a church through him.
Thomas will strengthen those converts and prepare them for the gathering.
Be patient in trials, don’t return insults, lead your home with meekness, and be steadfast — counsel Thomas later struggled with.

f.w: revile not against those that revile

n: Thomas will be a “physician” to the Church — he had studied medicine informally — but the world won’t accept him.

f.g: possibly literal (Thomas had some medical knowledge) and spiritual — healing souls in the Church.

n: He should go wherever the Lord sends him; the Holy Ghost will direct him.
Pray always to avoid temptation and keep your reward.

f.w: Pray always, lest you enter into temptation

n: Be faithful to the end; Christ is with him. These words come from Jesus Christ by the Father’s will.

f.w: not of man nor of men
